name: Recapio
subcategory: YouTube channel monitoring and daily AI recaps
tagline: Pick YouTube channels, get one daily email that distills every new upload into key takeaways.

pricing.notes: Pricing page is JS-rendered; tiers not captured at check time.

verdictSummary: For a handful of channels this is a genuine weekend build: poll each channel's uploads feed, pull the transcript of each new video, summarize with an LLM, email yourself one digest on a cron. The gaps are real. You are rebuilding a reliable transcript pipeline, which is the same YouTube-blocking problem that eats scrapers, you pay LLM costs per video, and you own the scheduling and deliverability. The editorial judgment of what is worth surfacing is the part that does not fall out of a prompt.
coreLoopDIY: Cron that checks a few channels' upload feeds, transcribes new videos, summarizes with an LLM, and emails you one digest.
requirements: a mail sender and a scheduler you keep running
whatYouLose: reliability of the transcript pipeline when YouTube rate-limits you
curation quality beyond a raw summarize prompt
email deliverability and scheduling you do not have to babysit
scaling past a few channels without cost and rate management
moatType: reliable transcript pipeline plus curation and delivery
whyPeopleStillPay: The demo is easy and the reliable version is not. Someone else eats the transcript-blocking problem, the LLM bill, the deliverability, and the daily judgment of what actually matters, so a working digest lands every morning without you operating anything.
notes: A personal version for a few channels is real; the reliable, curated, hands-off version is the product.
prompt: Build a personal YouTube channel digest as one Python script run on a daily cron. Stack: Python 3.11, the youtube-transcript-api library, an LLM SDK (OpenAI or Anthropic), and SMTP for email, no web UI. Read a list of channel IDs and your email from a .env. Each run: for every channel, find uploads from the last 24 hours via its RSS uploads feed, fetch each video's transcript, summarize it into 3 to 5 bullet takeaways with the LLM, and send one combined HTML email. Skip videos with no captions gracefully and never crash a run because one video failed. Cache processed video ids in a local JSON file so reruns do not duplicate. Include a README, a .env.example, and clear notes that transcript fetches can be rate-limited by YouTube and that LLM calls cost money per video. Deliberately out of scope: a web app, accounts, multi-user, and any paid transcript infrastructure.
